chunks: So they were rightly seized by a mighty blast; and We turned them into mouldy rubbish: A good riddance of the wicked people!

key_terms.الصَّيْحَةُ: The mighty cry or shout (often associated with Gabriel or the Angel of Death) that seizes people.
key_terms.بِالْحَقِّ: With the right/truth, indicating just and deserved punishment.
key_terms.غُثَاءً: Dry husk or rubbish, referring to the dried-out, hollow state of their bodies or souls.
key_terms.فَبُعْداً: So, away/away with them, a phrase of expulsion or doom.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'sayhah' and 'ghutha' in the context of divine punishment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the destruction of the people of Prophet Hud, where the 'cry' (sayhah) signifies a sudden, divine auditory signal that instantly annihilates the unjust. The transformation into 'ghutha' (dry husks) illustrates the complete loss of vitality and substance for those who rejected the truth, serving as a stern warning against arrogance. This event underscores the concept of divine retribution being both immediate and absolute for the oppressors.
